suffix: HEEWON STYLE: a Korean WEBTOON figure painted into a European OLD-MASTER canvas, composed like a Romanticist master painting. FIGURES are webtoon / anime: clean digital-ink linework, simplified webtoon faces with expressive eyes, shaded in soft watercolor washes and translucent oil glazes instead of flat cel fill — no skin pores, no photographic detail, not photoreal, not 3D. THE WORLD is painted with European old-master technique — Renaissance and Baroque oil (Titian, Rembrandt, Tiepolo, Turner): visible broken-colour brushwork, skies scumbled from short loaded dabs, layered glazes in the darks, sfumato edges, a touch of impasto on the brightest highlights — over watercolor wet-in-wet blooms, pigment granulation and faint paper grain; edges of the frame dissolve into paint. BACKGROUND AND FOREGROUND are a high-contrast Renaissance / Baroque TENEBRIST OIL PAINTING in their own right (Caravaggio, Georges de La Tour, Rembrandt, late Titian): a warm umber-to-black ground; walls, timber, stone, drapery, tables and the dark foreground shapes modelled in glazed oil and pulled out of the darkness by the one candle, lamp or window, with soft sfumato falloff into black — the webtoon figures are set INTO that old-master oil space, lit by the same key and sharing its shadows, never pasted onto a flat backdrop. LAYOUT is Romanticism (Delacroix, Géricault, Friedrich, Goya, Turner): heroic diagonal or pyramid composition, small figures against a sublime storm sky or vast field, extreme foreshortening (worm’s-eye from the dirt or straight down from above), one break in the clouds or one shaft as the key. LIGHT is movie tenebrism at full strength (Caravaggio, Rembrandt, night-interior cinema): an extreme value range — inky blacks right beside small near-white highlights, almost no middle grey; 70–80% of the frame in deep painted shadow (oil-glazed umber, indigo and black); ONE hard directional key (a lamp, a single cloud-break, a low sun shaft, firelight) carves the subject out of the dark. Form is modelled: the key wraps around cheekbones, armor plates, horse muscle and silk folds, then falls off at a hard terminator; a thin edge of that same real light grazes the far side of the silhouette to lift it off the background (never a glow outline); long raking shadows. Default hour is dusk, night, storm or pre-dawn — never flat overcast, never even daylight, never a bright open sky filling the frame. DEPTH is three planes in every still: a dark out-of-focus FOREGROUND shape near the lens (shoulder, rein, post, grass, smoke) framing the shot; the subject razor-sharp in the MIDGROUND; the BACKGROUND melting into soft wash and atmospheric haze, with round painted BOKEH discs wherever small lights sit behind the subject (lamps, torches, embers, sparks, rain, wet highlights). Shallow depth of field, overlapping shapes and receding haze so the frame goes back in space — never flat, never every plane in equal focus. SEPARATION: subject and background never share a value — a lit figure against a background pushed two steps darker, or a near-black silhouette against the one bright break; foreground shapes almost black; the eye lands on the subject first. COLOR SYMBOLISM reads at a glance: each kingdom's colour lives in its banners and cloth (Silla blue, Baekje yellow, Goguryeo red, Tang vermilion and gold), each named person's hex in the key light on them, and the rest of the frame stays desaturated umber, slate and black so those few colours sing. FACES stay drawn: match the attached portrait's line weight, eye shape and simplification exactly — if a face starts to read as a photograph, flatten it back to ink line and wash; extras are drawn the same way, never photographic. HORSES are drawn to be admired: the whole body readable, arched neck, deep chest, round haunch, clean legs in a true gait, muscle modelled by the key with a bright edge along the topline. 2D animated cel-painterly cinema, not photoreal, not live-action, not 3D CGI. Same film stock every still: a CAMERA in a real Korean place — anamorphic 2:1 movie frame, shallow DOF, creamy bokeh, rack-focus, film grain, crushed blacks, ONE hard key, long shadows, tenebrism. MOVIE FRAME of the scene a DP could stand in — NEVER a graphic poster, split-screen collage, 3D architectural visualization, black-triangle overlay, spotlight cone deleting the landscape, or neon outline. NO halo, bloom, glow aura, rim-aura, emissive skin, or god-ray envelope around people — character hex is the color of REAL LIGHT in the dark (key bounce, specular on silk/armor/wet stone, a lamp, a shaft, a floor reflection), never a body halo, never magic outline, never neon-painting the figure. FACE ONLY from the attached portrait — silk/hanbok may match; NEVER copy the portrait stance, clasped hands, 3/4 fashion lineup, or a standing clone. Invent a new DRAMATIC body every still (mid-stride, kneel, full-draw, turn, tumble, lean, count, dutch, worm’s-eye, lower-third). CINEMATOGRAPHY: name the shot — dutch angle, worm’s-eye, crane, over-shoulder, rack focus, shallow DOF / bokeh, chiaroscuro, mise-en-scène, long-shadow key. HIGH CONTRAST: crushed blacks + one hard key / long shadows / tenebrism — not even daylight wash, not a flat tourist postcard. ICONIC MINIMAL means one architectural device a lens can see (road, column, waterline, gate, hall axis) plus empty negative space — not deleting the world. COLOR SYMBOLISM: hex tints the hard key / catchlight / bounce — NEVER a glow aura, NEVER recolor the attached portrait’s garments (Sosuno stays dusty-rose hanbok, Geumwa stays red-burgundy court silk, not gold paint). FACE AND CLOTHES match the attached ch_*.png. One of each named person — NEVER clone or duplicate a character. People stand on packed earth at a well RIM — NEVER inside the well shaft. Jumong is fun-loving and laid-back: grin, laugh, wink, easy eyes — not a grim founder mask. BATTLE ARMOR: metallic GRAY steel lamellar (attached steel-armor ref); cloth peeks in the character hex — not gold-painted plate, not glowing armor, not a standing armor catalog. RING-POMMEL SWORDS: one-handed hip 환두대도 from attached sw_bidam.png — handle:blade 1:3; order is RING (pommel at heel of fist) → short grip → thin gold collar → long blade → point. Never reverse handle and blade. Never a tsuba disc in the middle. Never taller than the person. sword_*.png is a pommel ECU only — do not attach it on full-blade stills. Ignore swords on face portraits. Two people = two garment-true figures against crushed black. Real Korean architecture or a locked dark room. No army. No readable text. No watermark. Copy: dynamic poses in a mythology-scale layout; dramatic poses in a mythology-scale one-device layout; one hard key / chiaroscuro; one gesture in empty space — iconic and simple. Never: white / pale studio void as a room; earth places stay real buildings, not color-plane furniture; no pasted portrait pose — new body every still; no floating logo — still must be a movie frame of the scene; unrealistic layout, reptitive; real bottle-shaped Cheomseongdae plus a story beat.
